Attach a pedon to the references of the French Referentiel pedologique 2008

Source: R/key-rp2008.R
classify_rp2008.Rd

Attaches a PedonRecord to the references of the Referentiel pedologique 2008 (AFES; Baize and Girard coord.; Editions Quae, 2009). Experimental: this release tests the 110 references of the 34 groups of references (GER): alocrisols (2), andosols (6), anthroposols (5), arenosols (1), brunisols (2), the solums dominated by calcium or magnesium (7: rendosols, calcosols, dolomitosols, rendisols, calcisols, magnesisols, calcarisols), chernosols (3), colluviosols (1), cryosols (2), ferrallitisols and oxydisols (7), ferruginosols (4), fersialsols (4), fluviosols (4), grisols (3), gypsosols (2), histosols (5), leptismectisols (1), lithosols (1), luvisols (6), nitosols (1), organosols (4), pelosols (3), peyrosols (1), phaeosols (2), planosols (3), podzosols (8), rankosols (1), reductisols et redoxisols (3), regosols (1), salisols et sodisols (7), thalassosols (3), thiosols et sulfatosols (2), veracrisols (1) and vertisols (4). The horizons of the intertropical chapters (F, OX, RT, ND, FE, OXc, OXm) are read only in the intertropical domain, and the results of those chapters and of the nitosols say that the book calls them a first version (Q18); a fluviosol needs a recorded alluvial origin and is provisional while the position in the valley and the water table are not recorded (Q14). The histosols read their predominant H horizon between 40 and 120 cm, the luvisols their texture contrast by the bands of the chapter, the organosols the S/CEC of their Aho as a whole. The reductisols and redoxisols read the functional reductic or redox features starting within 50 cm and continuing over 50 cm (a G within 50 cm makes a reductisol whatever lies above), and their doubles with the luvisols, podzosols, pelosols, brunisols, colluviosols, cryosols and histosols are those the book names; the depth class of the hydromorphy is in trace$hydromorphy. The salisols and sodisols read the salic and sodic horizons within 60 cm, the thalassosols a recorded marine material (provisional while the tidal flooding or the polder is not recorded), the thiosols and sulfatosols, first in every case, the sulfur within 50 cm, the veracrisols their vermihumic Ah, the vertisols their SV and V, litho against topo by the site, else the SV.

Usage

classify_rp2008(
  pedon,
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

rules

Optional pre-loaded rules (load_rules("rp2008")).

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "rp2008": the main name in name ("[non rattache]" when nothing attaches), the GER label in rsg_or_order, the references in the name in levels (level "references", code, name, name_native, name_en, ger, attachment: simple, imperfect, simple_or_imperfect, double), every reference that may attach in candidates (with the columns of ClassificationResult, group the GER, plus name_en, implemented and precedence, the book's statements that put a reference of the name before it or exclude it), the evaluation of every reference, the horizon frame and the rapid key in trace (with trace$position, the depth of the first ND, OXm or OXc of a ferrallitisol or oxydisol and its proximal or distal type), and provisional_because ("references:<code>": the references or GER that could take the name once their data are known).

Details

The RP is not a key: a solum attaches to one, two or no reference, simply or imperfectly (pp. XIV, XVII). Every reference is tested every time: its sequences of reference horizons, matched on the horizon frame (the RP notation where the profile is written in it, else the horizons identified on the data, identify_horizons(pedon, "rp2008")), and the side tests of its chapter (depths, thicknesses, forbidden horizons, saturation, carbonates, permafrost, colluvial or anthropic materials). Each test is evaluated strictly and with the tolerances of p. 64 (depth and thickness 10 to 200 cm, pH +/- 0.2, CEC +/- 1, S/CEC +/- 5, organic carbon 8 +/- 2 and 30 +/- 5; any other threshold strict): a reference met only within tolerance, or by an imperfect case its chapter names (calcosol leptique, rendosol pachique, arenosol redoxique ...), is an imperfect attachment, never a simple one. The main name follows the book's explicit statements of precedence, then the degree, then the order of the rapid key (pp. 66-68); a double attachment is written only for the pairs the book prescribes (calcisol-calcosol, the anthroposols transformes); with no reference, the name is "[non rattache]" and the three nearest references are listed. The choice of one name is a convention of soilKey, and $candidates lists every reference that may attach the solum with its degree and the criteria that fail, pass only within tolerance or are undecided.

Names are French, as printed, in the singular (name, levels$name_native), with an English gloss (levels$name_en); the GER is a label (rsg_or_order, levels$ger), not a level. The qualifiers and the types come later. The readings where the text is silent are listed in system.file("rules", "rp2008", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

Baize D., Girard M.-C. (coord.) (2009). Referentiel pedologique 2008. AFES, Editions Quae, Versailles.

See also

make_rp2008_example, soilkey_systems, within_tolerance.

Examples

res <- classify_rp2008(make_rp2008_example("calcosols"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "calcosol"
res$candidates[, c("code", "degree", "in_name")]
#>        code degree in_name
#> 1 calcosols simple    TRUE
